lesson.name: The lesson
lesson.text: Young (Child) is having trouble learning (child.his/her) lessons. Today, (child.he/she) learned about the two factions that shaped Isola's history. "Like two friends, Magic and Nature share the island together," (teacher) said. "But long ago, they got into a terrible fight. They fought and fought for a long time, and their conflict almost cost them their lives. It took a lot of faith for them to rebuild their friendship. Yes, children, faith is important to life. For without faith, one cannot truly thrive."

essay.name: The essay
essay.text: (Child) has only two days to write an essay about what "faith" means to (child.him/her). But (child.he/she) doesn't really understand the topic. What should (child) write about?

choices.label: "Faith" means believing in the good of others
"Faith" means believing in a higher power

p1.text: Yes, "faith" must mean overcoming any problems {with a kind and patient heart|with maturity|with quiet courage|with strength}. (Child) scribbles down (child.his/her) thoughts and submits (child.his/her) work {MANNER}. (Teacher) is surprised at the amount of detail (child.he/she) included.

p2.text: Yes, "faith" must mean fighting for {what is correct|what you believe in}, even if {the world is against you|people don't always understand your perspective}. (Child) scribbles down (child.his/her) thoughts and submits (child.his/her) work {MANNER}. (Teacher) is surprised at the amount of detail (child.he/she) included.

p3.text: Yes, "faith" must mean thinking {the best of|highly of} others, {especially if they were former friends|because people have an innate goodness to them|because people might have made a mistake|because people are not as different as one thinks}. (Child) scribbles down (child.his/her) thoughts and submits (child.his/her) work {MANNER}. (Teacher) is surprised at the amount of detail (child.he/she) included.

p4.text: Yes, "faith" must mean that {there is something supernatural in control of one's life|there is something natural guiding one's life|there is something magical influencing the world|there are spirits watching over Isola|there is a god|there are gods|there is a guiding hand|there is something or someone watching over us}. Or perhaps {POWERS} have more control over one's life than one thinks. Or maybe {nothing is in control|nothing apparent is guiding our lives|one must take charge of one's own destiny}! Whatever the case, (child) believes that people must {respect the world around them|respect other people's beliefs|take charge of their own destiny|listen to those who guide them|believe what they want to believe|think for themselves}. (Child) scribbles down (child.his/her) thoughts and submits (child.his/her) work {MANNER}. (Teacher) is surprised at the amount of detail (child.he/she) included.

p5.text: (Child) remains stumped by the cryptic question. There are a lot of things "faith" could refer to and (child.he/she) can't decide. Well, except for one thing: if (child.he/she) can't decide on a single thing, perhaps it means that "faith" means something different to different people. (child.He/She) decides to write (child.his/her) thoughts down and turns in the paper {MANNER}. (Teacher) is surprised at the amount of detail (child.he/she) included and at (child.his/her) {cheekiness|utter defiance|refusal to answer the question|cleverness|intelligence|ability to think outside of the box}.

p6.text: (Child) remains stumped by the cryptic question. There are a lot of things "faith" could refer to and (child.he/she) can't decide. Well, except for one thing: the question itself must have no right answer. Why ask it in such a vague way, then? (child.He/She) decides to write (child.his/her) thoughts down and turns in the paper {MANNER}. (Teacher) is surprised at the amount of detail (child.he/she) included and at (child.his/her) {cheekiness|utter defiance|refusal to answer the question|cleverness|intelligence|ability to think outside of the box}.

Although (teacher) isn't entirely convinced, (teacher.he/she) gives (child) partial credit for making an effort. Better luck next time!

g6.text: (Child) gets (child.his/her) paper back with an unusual note: "Interesting! Come see me after class." Hmm. What could that mean? After class, (teacher) asks (child) why (child.he/she) chose to write about faith that way. The two discuss their ideas, and (teacher) {agrees with some of (child.his/her) points|admits that (teacher.he/she) hadn't considered that perspective before|asks a few more questions}. By the end, (child) has learned something new. Perhaps (teacher) has, too!

see_me.name: See me after class
see_me.text:
After some time, (child) gets (child.his/her) paper back.
(child) sees that (teacher) has written a "See Me After Class" note on (child.his/her) work. Not knowing what to expect, (child.he/she) sits down at (teacher)'s desk. (teacher) {smiles|raises an eyebrow|chuckles softly|looks rather serious} and...

praise.text: praises (child) for {PRAISE}. (teacher.He/She) says, "You raise an interesting point. Faith does not necessarily mean being forced into one single answer. It could mean the ability to question everything around us. One must use one's own brain and heart to come to an answer. Whether your answer is right or wrong is not always up to me. It is up to you to think about what you believe, and why."

coda.text: (child) ponders (teacher)'s words. Although (child.he/she) doesn't fully grasp (teacher)'s wisdom now, the words remain with (child.him/her) and guide (child.him/her) as (child.he/she) grows up. (child.He/She) eventually becomes a wise young (child.man/woman), displaying wisdom far beyond (child.his/her) years.
